independence: Built from the read-only upstream Git objects first. The 2026-08-07 review and consensus were consulted only to attach current local decisions; no source, live, independent, or joined census was read.

atom_contract.rule: one trigger, one observable effect, one independently degradable behavior
atom_contract.range_basis: one-indexed inclusive lines in the exact HEAD blob
atom_contract.blob_rule: Every atom repeats HEAD commit, path, range, and a blob alias whose OID, SHA-256, byte count, and LF EOF are frozen below.

decision_basis.status: recommendations only; no adoption or activation is implied by this census

atoms.trigger: During TDD, the public interface or seam shape is itself unsettled.
atoms.observable_effect: Consult codebase-design vocabulary as a reference without starting a separate workflow session.
atoms.independent_degradation: A literal slash pointer can be reachable in Claude while dangling in Codex, or can accidentally start a second process instead of loading vocabulary.
atoms.decision_evidence: No local seam-failure sample shows benefit; first real seam ambiguity must prove shared catalog reach and reference-only loading in both harnesses.

atoms.trigger: A debugging run is about to show a command, output, or captured artifact.
atoms.observable_effect: Every secret is replaced with a redaction marker before it is shown.
atoms.independent_degradation: Masking only later prose still leaves raw tool output or transcripts exposed.
atoms.decision_evidence: This is the highest-priority safety increment, but it must be enforced at the producing command or script, not merely copied as prose.

atoms.trigger: A feedback loop needs authenticated access.
atoms.observable_effect: The credential remains in an environment variable instead of appearing in the displayed command.
atoms.independent_degradation: Command arguments or shell expansion can leak credential values even if later artifacts are redacted.
atoms.decision_evidence: Local systematic-debugging has source commands that expose values; those producers must be changed and canary-tested in Claude and Codex.

atoms.trigger: A captured trace contains authentication headers or other sensitive context.
atoms.observable_effect: Only the lines carrying the diagnostic signal are quoted.
atoms.independent_degradation: A minimally useful quote can still become a wholesale artifact disclosure if selection is not enforced.
atoms.decision_evidence: Port the least-data rule into the existing debug skill and verify raw artifact, transcript, and final report surfaces.

atoms.trigger: Redacted evidence is insufficient to diagnose the bug.
atoms.observable_effect: The agent states the limitation and asks the user instead of exposing more data or guessing.
atoms.independent_degradation: A run may either leak more context or continue on an underdetermined diagnosis.
atoms.decision_evidence: Keep as the safe degradation path after source-side filtering; it does not replace the filter.

atoms.trigger: A human-in-the-loop reproduction requires authentication.
atoms.observable_effect: Signing in is a human step; only non-secret observations should be captured for the agent.
atoms.independent_degradation: Using capture for login or credentials prints the value back to the terminal and agent.
atoms.decision_evidence: Retain the principle but harden the local template so allowed capture fields are explicit and mechanically scrubbed.

atoms.trigger: The example HITL flow asks a user to paste an error message.
atoms.observable_effect: The entered free text is printed verbatim as captured output.
atoms.independent_degradation: Secrets embedded in an error string bypass the prose-only redaction instruction.
atoms.decision_evidence: This HEAD counterexample proves upstream redaction is not mechanically complete; do not copy the template unchanged.
atoms.delta_relation: HEAD limitation exposed by new safety contract

atoms.trigger: An agent edits a skill, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent-consumed document.
atoms.observable_effect: The renamed skill is model-reachable and applies one writing discipline across those document forms.
atoms.independent_degradation: Installing the whole skill adds a competing authoring authority and a new routing surface.
atoms.decision_evidence: Reuse only the novel doctrine in the existing skill-authoring source of truth; do not install this skill.

atoms.trigger: A required document is kept outside always-loaded context.
atoms.observable_effect: The pointer names both the material and each distinct branch that should retrieve it, with trigger language front-loaded and deduplicated.
atoms.independent_degradation: A valid target behind weak wording is not loaded reliably.
atoms.decision_evidence: luca_gstack already uses pointer-first governance and explicit routing; no independent module is justified.
atoms.delta_relation: generalized from skill descriptions to all pointers

atoms.trigger: A vague completion bound demonstrably causes premature completion.
atoms.observable_effect: Later steps are hidden only by a true handoff or subagent context boundary after sharpening the bound fails.
atoms.independent_degradation: An inline call leaves later steps visible and cannot deliver the claimed attention isolation.
atoms.decision_evidence: Existing Plan/subagent/checkpoint contracts already supply real boundaries and executable completion gates.

atoms.trigger: An agent document is about to restate a command, config, directory fact, or tool help that the environment can reveal cheaply.
atoms.observable_effect: The environment remains authoritative; prose caches only facts that are costly or impossible to recover by inspection.
atoms.independent_degradation: Restated cheap facts drift from executable reality and become stale instructions.
atoms.decision_evidence: Add one sentence to the existing skill-authoring authority and point both harness contracts to it; no duplicate prose.

atoms.trigger: Two user-only skills need the same reference but cannot invoke one another.
atoms.observable_effect: The shared reference is placed in a plain external file both can point to.
atoms.independent_degradation: Duplicating the reference in each skill causes semantic drift; pretending one user-only skill can fire the other causes a dead edge.
atoms.decision_evidence: The framework already centralizes contracts in skill-os files and exposes them by pointers.

atoms.trigger: Human cognitive load from many user-only skills becomes too high.
atoms.observable_effect: A user-only router lists candidate skills but cannot autonomously invoke another user-only skill.
atoms.independent_degradation: Treating the router as an execution engine creates unreachable or falsely claimed dispatch.
atoms.decision_evidence: luca_gstack's route-guard and harness adapters have different explicit dispatch contracts; do not import this limitation as a universal rule.

atoms.trigger: The open question concerns business logic, state transitions, or data shape rather than visual appearance.
atoms.observable_effect: The prototype router chooses a non-visual logic demo branch and discloses ambiguity assumptions.
atoms.independent_degradation: Routing it into a polished visual prototype spends the wrong constraints and obscures the state-model question.
atoms.decision_evidence: The sliver is real but has no local demand sample; first true logic-only task gets a one-off demo, not a new skill, route, mode, or gap.
atoms.delta_relation: logic branch changed from terminal app to HTML demo

atoms.trigger: A logic demo is about to be authored.
atoms.observable_effect: The exact state model and question appear visibly at the top of the demo.
atoms.independent_degradation: A correct-looking artifact can answer a different question without a checkable statement of intent.
atoms.decision_evidence: Retain as a pilot acceptance condition only after real demand.
atoms.delta_relation: changed from README/comment to visible intro

atoms.trigger: The state-model behavior is implemented for the demo.
atoms.observable_effect: The logic lives as a small pure module in one script block that can be lifted into production separately from the page.
atoms.independent_degradation: Embedding rules in UI handlers makes the learned behavior non-portable.
atoms.decision_evidence: Use as the primary pilot seam, not as authorization to alter the existing visual prototype chain.
atoms.delta_relation: changed host from project runtime module to inline pure module

atoms.trigger: A reducer, state machine, functions, or stateful module is selected for the question.
atoms.observable_effect: The page calls the logic through a clean interface; logic never references DOM objects or handlers.
atoms.independent_degradation: DOM coupling makes a visually working demo unusable as validated logic.
atoms.decision_evidence: Require a source-level isolation check in any future one-off pilot.
atoms.delta_relation: changed shell isolation from terminal I/O to DOM isolation

atoms.trigger: The logic demo must be shareable with a non-developer.
atoms.observable_effect: One inline HTML/CSS/JS file opens by double-click with no framework, bundler, or server.
atoms.independent_degradation: A runtime or install requirement removes the shareable-demo property.
atoms.decision_evidence: This is the candidate artifact shape for a future real logic-only case, not a default framework output.
atoms.delta_relation: replaced TUI runtime with self-contained HTML

atoms.trigger: A non-developer reads or drives the logic demo.
atoms.observable_effect: Labels and explanations use domain language rather than reducer or code vocabulary.
atoms.independent_degradation: The model may be technically testable yet opaque to the decision holder.
atoms.decision_evidence: Already consonant with product-neutral CONTEXT vocabulary; only validate in a real pilot.

atoms.trigger: Any demo action changes the model.
atoms.observable_effect: The full relevant state is re-rendered as labelled fields and the change can be called out.
atoms.independent_degradation: Partial or raw-JSON state hides illegal or surprising transitions.
atoms.decision_evidence: Make this an observable pilot criterion, not a new permanent UI rule.
atoms.delta_relation: translated terminal frame behavior to readable HTML state

atoms.trigger: A reviewer wants to explore unplanned action orderings.
atoms.observable_effect: Every action remains available as a free-play button and dispatches through the state model.
atoms.independent_degradation: Guided cases alone can miss emergent illegal sequences.
atoms.decision_evidence: Validate with state-transition oracles if a real pilot occurs.

atoms.trigger: A reviewer chooses a happy, edge, or illegal walkthrough.
atoms.observable_effect: A tabbed ordered scenario resets to known state and advances through real action buttons deterministically.
atoms.independent_degradation: A walkthrough that does not reset or uses fake steps cannot be reproduced or compared.
atoms.decision_evidence: Keep as a future pilot criterion; no route or framework mutation now.

atoms.trigger: The prototype has answered its question.
atoms.observable_effect: Validated logic is absorbed separately while the disposable HTML shell remains only as a rerunnable primary-source artifact.
atoms.independent_degradation: Shipping the shell or discarding the validated module confuses evidence with production implementation.
atoms.decision_evidence: Local prototype governance differs; any pilot must map this separation to the existing project artifact and handoff rules.
atoms.delta_relation: updated capture mapping for HTML shell

atoms.trigger: Several decision-tree nodes have all prerequisites settled.
atoms.observable_effect: The entire current frontier is asked in one numbered round, then the agent waits for the round's answers.
atoms.independent_degradation: Batching can overwhelm the user and bypass the local one-decision sharpening rhythm even if dependency ordering is correct.
atoms.decision_evidence: Upstream graduation does not satisfy the local restart gate of two real impatience incidents after narrow-to-two fails.
atoms.delta_relation: batch-grill behavior merged into stable grilling

atoms.trigger: A frontier question is presented inside a round.
atoms.observable_effect: Each question has a fixed numbered title/body format and an attached recommended answer.
atoms.independent_degradation: Formatting can pass while the number or cognitive breadth of simultaneous questions remains harmful.
atoms.decision_evidence: No local A/B shows this batch presentation improves decisions; structured question tools also cap short parallel questions.

atoms.trigger: An answer settles decisions and may unlock dependent questions.
atoms.observable_effect: The frontier is recomputed; any question depending on another still-open question moves to a later round.
atoms.independent_degradation: A complete batch can still ask logically premature questions if dependency recalculation fails.
atoms.decision_evidence: The dependency rule is sound but inseparable from a locally rejected whole-frontier interaction without a bounded adaptation trial.

atoms.trigger: One frontier question depends on a discoverable environmental fact.
atoms.observable_effect: A subagent finds the fact while unrelated frontier questions proceed; only dependent questions wait.
atoms.independent_degradation: A failed or unavailable subagent can silently turn a fact into a user question or block the whole round.
atoms.decision_evidence: The fact/decision split already exists locally; adopting it through the rejected round protocol adds no independent value.

atoms.trigger: No decision-tree frontier remains.
atoms.observable_effect: The interview still does not act until the user confirms shared understanding.
atoms.independent_degradation: An empty machine frontier can falsely stand in for human agreement.
atoms.decision_evidence: The human confirmation invariant is already mandatory; it does not justify the round migration.
atoms.delta_relation: completion gate carried into promoted grilling

atoms.trigger: A triage item needs grilling to become actionable.
atoms.observable_effect: Triage now asks a round of questions at a time rather than one question at a time.
atoms.independent_degradation: The core skill can be rejected locally while a consumer silently preserves the same batch behavior.
atoms.decision_evidence: Any adoption ledger must account for consuming sites; local triage must not inherit rejected rounds indirectly.

atoms.trigger: A workflow-spec interview runs through loop-me.
atoms.observable_effect: The consumer explicitly uses rounds of questions with a recommendation attached to each.
atoms.independent_degradation: Deleting only the standalone batch skill leaves identical behavior active in downstream consumers.
atoms.decision_evidence: No local counterpart is installed; record lineage only and do not introduce a route.

atoms.trigger: A user explicitly chooses the questionnaire capability in Claude-style packaging.
atoms.observable_effect: The promoted skill remains user-invoked and is not autonomously selected by the model.
atoms.independent_degradation: Promotion alone can be mistaken for permission to add an automatic route.
atoms.decision_evidence: Graduation lowers upstream maturity uncertainty but does not replace local demand evidence.
atoms.delta_relation: renamed path from in-progress to productivity with body preserved

atoms.trigger: The questionnaire package is discovered by Codex.
atoms.observable_effect: Codex metadata explicitly disallows implicit invocation.
atoms.independent_degradation: Claude-only frontmatter parity can pass while Codex still invokes the skill automatically.
atoms.decision_evidence: Any future pilot remains natural-language or explicit user-selected and must not create a new registered route.

atoms.trigger: The user needs knowledge held by another named person.
atoms.observable_effect: The interview asks only about the send and shapes document questions around the knowledge gap.
atoms.independent_degradation: Re-interviewing the user about facts they do not have cannot produce the missing evidence.
atoms.decision_evidence: The first real named-recipient case may use this as a one-off artifact, separated from research-kit discovery outputs.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: A questionnaire send is proposed.
atoms.observable_effect: One exchange resolves the recipient's role, expertise, relationship, and unique knowledge before drafting.
atoms.independent_degradation: Without a concrete recipient, tone and assumed context are fabricated.
atoms.decision_evidence: Missing recipient remains a blocking human gate in any pilot.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: The recipient is known.
atoms.observable_effect: One exchange produces the concrete facts or decisions the user must receive back.
atoms.independent_degradation: A known recipient without a decision target yields a generic survey instead of a decision instrument.
atoms.decision_evidence: Missing return requirement remains a blocking human gate in any pilot.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: Recipient and required return are both known.
atoms.observable_effect: A named Markdown artifact is written in the current directory and every required return is covered by at least one question.
atoms.independent_degradation: An unpinned current directory can mis-scope the write even when question coverage passes.
atoms.decision_evidence: A future one-off must write through the pinned project path and cannot copy the current-directory rule literally.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: The one-off questionnaire is drafted.
atoms.observable_effect: Questions are ordered most-important-first and grouped by theme only when numerous.
atoms.independent_degradation: An async recipient may answer only an early portion, making weak ordering materially lossy.
atoms.decision_evidence: Use as a pilot acceptance condition only; no registration change.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: An individual questionnaire item is authored.
atoms.observable_effect: Each question asks one idea, includes an immediate answer stub, and adds rationale only when misunderstanding is likely.
atoms.independent_degradation: Compound questions or detached answer areas reduce completion and attribution quality.
atoms.decision_evidence: Use as a one-off document quality check after the two human gates.
atoms.delta_relation: unchanged body exposed by stable graduation

atoms.trigger: The agent encounters provisioning, credentials, an unfamiliar dashboard, migration, or cutover that requires human-only steps.
atoms.observable_effect: The promoted skill may invoke itself and generate an interactive Bash procedure.
atoms.independent_degradation: An automatic credential or cutover trigger can cross human, account, repository, and irreversible-action gates without explicit authorization.
atoms.decision_evidence: Only reconsider after at least two repeated manual setup needs and then require a user-invoked, mocked, rollback-capable local design.

atoms.trigger: Codex indexes the graduated wizard metadata.
atoms.observable_effect: The metadata exposes the wizard without an explicit no-implicit-invocation policy.
atoms.independent_degradation: Claude and Codex can diverge in automatic activation semantics even when both display the skill.
atoms.decision_evidence: The missing Codex deny is incompatible with the required user-controlled dangerous-operation boundary.
atoms.delta_relation: new Codex metadata without implicit-invocation deny

atoms.trigger: A human-only procedure is being scoped.
atoms.observable_effect: The agent enumerates ordered stages and maps each captured value to source, destination, and secret/public status, then asks for confirmation.
atoms.independent_degradation: A complete stage list can still target the wrong account or repository if identity is not pinned separately.
atoms.decision_evidence: Useful planning discipline does not cure missing transaction identity, rollback, and per-write approval.
atoms.delta_relation: existing behavior newly exposed by promotion

atoms.trigger: A stage depends on a third-party UI or command path.
atoms.observable_effect: The path is made concrete from repository or documentation evidence; unknown steps are disclosed rather than invented.
atoms.independent_degradation: A correct stage schema can still send the human through a stale or nonexistent external interface.
atoms.decision_evidence: The rule is necessary but insufficient for safe external mutation and does not warrant installation.
atoms.delta_relation: existing behavior newly exposed by promotion

atoms.trigger: The approved procedure is authored.
atoms.observable_effect: Only dependency-ordered stages below a fixed template marker are customized.
atoms.independent_degradation: Treating the library as immutable can preserve unsafe helpers and hides version or local-policy changes.
atoms.decision_evidence: A local design would require an audited library and transaction contract, not byte-faith in the upstream template.
atoms.delta_relation: existing behavior newly exposed by promotion

atoms.trigger: A generated stage contains an irreversible action.
atoms.observable_effect: The author is instructed to place a confirmation gate before that action.
atoms.independent_degradation: Reversible external writes and credential changes still occur without per-write preview, confirmation, or compensation.
atoms.decision_evidence: A single prose gate cannot provide the required transaction semantics.
atoms.delta_relation: existing behavior newly exposed by promotion

atoms.trigger: The generated script is ready for verification.
atoms.observable_effect: Syntax and optional shellcheck run, but the procedure is not executed end-to-end; value flow is traced statically.
atoms.independent_degradation: External-write, quoting, rollback, account, and cancellation faults remain untested.
atoms.decision_evidence: Static trace cannot substitute for mocked execution and rollback fixtures.
atoms.delta_relation: existing behavior newly exposed by promotion

atoms.trigger: A stage names an external dashboard URL.
atoms.observable_effect: The script attempts platform-specific browser openers and falls back to a manual URL warning.
atoms.independent_degradation: Opening the right URL does not pin account, tenant, or repository identity.
atoms.decision_evidence: External GUI side effects must remain user-operated and identity-bound in any future design.

atoms.trigger: A stage requests a visible or secret value and an existing environment file may already contain it.
atoms.observable_effect: The script reads the existing value, offers reuse, hides newly typed secrets, and stores the result in a shell variable.
atoms.independent_degradation: Secret existence and content cross from disk into process memory without identity, permission, or redaction guarantees.
atoms.decision_evidence: Hidden input is not equivalent to safe storage or account-scoped authorization.

atoms.trigger: A captured value is marked for local persistence.
atoms.observable_effect: The script rewrites the selected environment file through a temporary file and records the key as written.
atoms.independent_degradation: There is no backup, rollback, gitignore preflight, escaping contract, or per-write approval; embedded newlines can corrupt the file.
atoms.decision_evidence: The upstream idempotence claim is not a recoverability proof.

atoms.trigger: A captured value is mapped to a GitHub Actions secret or variable.
atoms.observable_effect: The script writes through gh when authenticated, otherwise records the operation as skipped.
atoms.independent_degradation: Authentication can point at the wrong account or repository, and a partial set of writes has no compensating rollback.
atoms.decision_evidence: External mutation requires explicit target identity, preview, per-write confirmation, mock tests, and compensation.

atoms.trigger: The wizard reaches its finish function after any mix of writes and skips.
atoms.observable_effect: It summarizes local writes, GitHub secrets, and skipped actions.
atoms.independent_degradation: A friendly summary can normalize a partially committed state without rollback or an explicit failed transaction status.
atoms.decision_evidence: Partial success must be journaled and compensated, not merely reported.

atoms.trigger: One work phase has actually ended and the next is about to start.
atoms.observable_effect: Context continuation, clearing, handoff, subagent, or compaction is chosen only at the boundary; mid-phase work continues or branches to a subagent.
atoms.independent_degradation: Applying the tree mid-phase discards the live reasoning thread.
atoms.decision_evidence: The boundary invariant is sound but current checkpoint and session contracts already cover it.

atoms.trigger: The next phase needs verbatim primary-source reasoning or is estimated to fit in a roughly 150k-token smart zone.
atoms.observable_effect: The same session continues and preserves full context.
atoms.independent_degradation: The hard-coded window estimate and manual judgement are model- and harness-specific and can override actual compaction behavior.
atoms.decision_evidence: Do not import a fixed token threshold; actual harness continuation and durable checkpoints remain authoritative.

atoms.trigger: All current exploration, decisions, and dead ends are irrelevant to the next phase.
atoms.observable_effect: The context is cleared while the old session remains resumable.
atoms.independent_degradation: A Claude slash assumption is not portable to Codex, and a mistaken relevance judgement irreversibly loses the why.
atoms.decision_evidence: Harness-native session management cannot be encoded as a shared literal slash branch.

atoms.trigger: Work moves to another harness, directory, colleague, or a mid-phase side task.
atoms.observable_effect: A portable Markdown handoff is produced only for those four travel cases.
atoms.independent_degradation: This narrow definition conflicts with lucagstack's durable mandatory handoff artifacts and shared state semantics.
atoms.decision_evidence: Do not weaken local handoffs to portability-only or encode Claude slash behavior in the shared framework.

atoms.trigger: The next task is tight enough to complete without user steering.
atoms.observable_effect: It is delegated to a subagent while the parent session stays intact.
atoms.independent_degradation: Prompt-only scope can be falsely treated as execution isolation or completion proof.
atoms.decision_evidence: Native multi-agent delegation already exists with stronger ownership and verification contracts.

atoms.trigger: Context is relevant, work stays in the same harness and directory, and human steering remains necessary after cheaper branches fail.
atoms.observable_effect: A slash compaction with a next-phase instruction becomes the default fallback.
atoms.independent_degradation: Codex does not expose this slash contract, while both harnesses already perform automatic compaction differently.
atoms.decision_evidence: The local contract explicitly avoids prescribing manual compaction as a shared workflow step.

atoms.trigger: A context-moving option other than Continue is considered.
atoms.observable_effect: The decision explicitly trades primary-source information for less noise and more room.
atoms.independent_degradation: Treating every handoff or compaction as equally lossy ignores structured durable artifacts and native session receipts.
atoms.decision_evidence: Retain the general lossiness awareness; reject the upstream tree and its equivalence claims.

atoms.trigger: The user explicitly invokes the corrective because the previous message did not land.
atoms.observable_effect: The skill is user-only in Claude-style packaging.
atoms.independent_degradation: A dedicated corrective command increases cognitive and routing load for a trigger already expressed in natural language.
atoms.decision_evidence: The user's ordinary request to explain or speak plainly is sufficient.

atoms.trigger: Codex discovers the corrective package.
atoms.observable_effect: Metadata explicitly prevents implicit invocation.
atoms.independent_degradation: Adding the registration still spends catalog and human-index cost despite correct invocation parity.
atoms.decision_evidence: No registered Codex skill is needed for an ordinary conversational correction.

atoms.trigger: The last answer was not understood.
atoms.observable_effect: The answer is re-pitched with enough missing context to orient the user.
atoms.independent_degradation: A rephrasing can remain opaque if it merely adds more explanation without changing the mental model.
atoms.decision_evidence: Already required by ordinary assistant behavior and office voice; do not register a skill.

atoms.trigger: The previous answer must be simplified.
atoms.observable_effect: The rewrite is constrained to ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
atoms.independent_degradation: An English technical-writing standard does not guarantee clarity in Chinese and can distort natural product language.
atoms.decision_evidence: Use the user's language and direct plain wording instead of importing the English-specific standard.

atoms.trigger: A misunderstood answer is re-pitched inside a project.
atoms.observable_effect: The rewrite uses the ubiquitous language in CONTEXT.md.
atoms.independent_degradation: A missing or stale context file can replace the user's current words with outdated jargon.
atoms.decision_evidence: Project vocabulary loading is already a mandatory framework contract with a user-language fallback.

atoms.trigger: A two-axis code review reaches its parallel review step.
atoms.observable_effect: The behavior is stated as spawning two subagents in parallel without naming a vendor tool or agent type.
atoms.independent_degradation: A heading can remain portable while the local harness lacks the required role, isolation, or receipt mechanics.
atoms.decision_evidence: The direction is correct, but generic prose does not prove Codex or Claude dispatch; local role wiring must be verified separately.

atoms.trigger: A selected deepening candidate needs alternative interfaces.
atoms.observable_effect: Three or more parallel subagents each produce a radically different design without a named vendor tool.
atoms.independent_degradation: The source may be portable while Codex catalog reach, nested references, or native parallel dispatch is absent.
atoms.decision_evidence: Migrate the complete codebase-design directory to the shared skill root, retain Claude compatibility, and verify real dispatch in both harnesses before exposing the TDD pointer.

atoms.trigger: An architecture scan begins exploration.
atoms.observable_effect: A subagent explores the codebase without hard-coding Claude's Agent/Explore names.
atoms.independent_degradation: Removing a vendor name can still leave an unavailable capability or unsafe write-enabled explorer.
atoms.decision_evidence: No local installed counterpart is being refreshed in this cycle; record the adaptation pattern only.

atoms.trigger: A Claude Code user installs the upstream collection.
atoms.observable_effect: The official marketplace plugin installs a managed read-only bundle and receives automatic updates.
atoms.independent_degradation: Automatic upstream updates bypass lucagstack's pinned source review, adaptation, and gated activation.
atoms.decision_evidence: Keep the local registry, watcher, and fusion control layer; do not install or subscribe the framework to the plugin.

atoms.trigger: A Codex or other Agent-Skills user installs upstream skills.
atoms.observable_effect: skills.sh copies selected editable skill files and prompts the installer to include setup-matt-pocock-skills.
atoms.independent_degradation: A copied file can bypass local lineage pins, local modifications, and dual-harness acceptance gates.
atoms.decision_evidence: Continue governed source ingestion rather than direct installer adoption.

atoms.trigger: A user chooses how to consume the upstream collection.
atoms.observable_effect: Managed plugin and editable-copy routes are declared mutually exclusive to avoid duplicate skills.
atoms.independent_degradation: luca_gstack deliberately has shared truth plus harness adapters, so copying this rule literally would misclassify its architecture.
atoms.decision_evidence: Record as upstream distribution lineage only; it is not a local architecture rule.

atoms.trigger: A human-facing skill page is authored where the site renderer already owns install UI.
atoms.observable_effect: The page omits duplicate install commands and changes the canonical renderer block instead.
atoms.independent_degradation: Hand-written copies drift from the executable or rendered source of truth.
atoms.decision_evidence: The reusable principle is fully captured by the adopted environment/cache doctrine.

atoms.trigger: A Common questions section is considered for a skill page.
atoms.observable_effect: Real questions are sought from the wiki, issues, and changelog; section length remains proportional to evidence.
atoms.independent_degradation: Invented padding can satisfy structure while answering questions no user has.
atoms.decision_evidence: This is upstream page-authoring process, not a missing lucagstack runtime capability.

atoms.trigger: A human-facing page claims how to tell a skill works.
atoms.observable_effect: Each signal must be checkable from the user's work or visible trace without inspecting the skill source.
atoms.independent_degradation: An internal compliance check can masquerade as a user-observable outcome.
atoms.decision_evidence: Existing quality gates already distinguish evidence from file existence; no new module is warranted.

atoms.trigger: A page presents a multi-way choice.
atoms.observable_effect: Branches are represented as a list or table rather than embedded in a paragraph.
atoms.independent_degradation: Correct branch prose can remain hard to scan and easy to miss.
atoms.decision_evidence: The local routing and planning contracts already use structured maps and tables where branches matter.

atoms.trigger: An upstream skill is retired.
atoms.observable_effect: The deprecated bucket is emptied and retired skills are deleted, with replacement lineage delegated to changesets.
atoms.independent_degradation: A blind refresh could either resurrect removed upstream skills or delete unrelated local capabilities with similar names.
atoms.decision_evidence: The four deprecated and two personal removals have no installed or adopted local counterpart; record the removals, perform no deletion.
atoms.delta_relation: bucket policy changed and removals applied

scope broadened from skills to all agent-consumed documents and model invocation enabled
